audit.whatIsWrong: The entry says 'Warwick's entire damage model is auto-attack on-hit, and one Blinding Dart erases that window.' Jaws of the Beast (Q) is a targeted lunge, not a basic attack.
audit.why: Blind stops basic attacks and the Eternal Hunger on-hit that rides them. It does not stop a spell cast. Q deals damage based on your maximum health and heals him for it, so a blinded Warwick standing in 365 range still trades and still sustains.
audit.corrected: Blind kills his autos and Eternal Hunger; Jaws of the Beast still lands and still heals through it. Leaving his 365-unit lunge range is the actual answer.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl (E) is never mentioned anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: It is 2.5 seconds of flat damage reduction followed by a 1-second flee on nearby enemies. Against Teemo that is both a burst-eater during your poke window and a forced disengage that pushes you out of Toxic Shot range at the exact moment your poison is stacking — and it is his answer to being poked at low HP.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl blunts your poke for 2.5s and then fears you off him; 15s at rank 1 falling to 11s at rank 5, against your flat 7s Blinding Dart.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. Both layers said 'track his R' without a single number.
audit.why: Every number here is decisive and known: Infinite Duress 110/90/70, Primal Howl 15/14/13/12/11, Jaws of the Beast 8s down to 6s, Blood Hunt 80s down to 40s, and Blinding Dart a flat 7s at every rank. Teemo's blind cycles roughly twice per Primal Howl and many times per R.
audit.corrected: Wait for Primal Howl (15s at rank 1) before you commit a poke chain, and treat R at 110s as a whole-wave permission slip rather than a single trade window.

audit.why: Anti-heal emphasis is right and matches the missing-interactions flag: Eternal Hunger, Jaws of the Beast and Infinite Duress all heal, and the passive healing triples below 25% HP.

edits.before: At level 1 you have the clearest edge in the game: Warwick's entire damage model is auto-attack on-hit, and one Blinding Shot (Q) erases that window. Walk up on every last-hit he goes for, land the auto-poison stack from Toxic Shot (E), and blind him the instant he tries to trade back. The problem is his passive: he heals hardest below 50% HP, so a Warwick you've poked down suddenly becomes faster and harder to finish — resist the urge to all-in a low-HP Warwick at level 1-2 without ignite or the kill is going to swing back on you. Buy Oblivion Orb as your first back item if you can; without anti-heal, his Jaws of the Beast (Q) heals enough to undo two or three poke patterns per wave.
edits.after: At level 1 you have the clearest edge in the game: Warwick's walk-up damage is basic attacks, and one Blinding Dart (Q) erases that window along with the Eternal Hunger on-hit riding it. Walk up on every last-hit he goes for, land the auto-poison stack from Toxic Shot (E), and blind him the instant he tries to trade back. Two things break that plan. Jaws of the Beast (Q) is a targeted lunge, not an auto — Blind does nothing to it and it heals him for max-health damage — so step outside 365 units after you blind. And his passive heals hardest below 50% HP, so a poked-down Warwick gets harder to finish, not easier: do not all-in a low Warwick at level 1-2 without Ignite. Buy Oblivion Orb first back.

edits.before: From level 4 onward the lane becomes genuinely contested. Your Q cooldown is dropping and shrooms are expanding your zone control, but Warwick hits level 6 in this window and Infinite Duress changes every equation. His R is a suppress — it bypasses Blind, holds you in place, and lets him heal the entire channel duration through your poison stack without taking a single auto-attack penalty. Track his R exactly the way a Darius player tracks Apprehend: if it is down, you play aggressively and run your full poke loop; if it is up, you respect 50% HP as your hard stop, back off into camouflage (passive), and never let him get within dash range. Shroom the brush at the river entrance and tribush so Blood Hunt (W) speed does not let him sneak into your blind spot.
edits.after: From level 4 onward the lane becomes genuinely contested. Your Q is a flat 7 seconds at every rank while Primal Howl (E) is 15 seconds at rank 1, so you get roughly two blinds per howl — that is the sequencing that matters before level 6. Wait for Primal Howl before you start a poke chain, because its 2.5s of damage reduction eats your burst and the flee that follows drags you out of Toxic Shot range. Then Infinite Duress lands and changes every equation: R is a suppress, it bypasses Blind, holds you, and heals him the entire channel. Track it at 110 seconds on rank 1 — if it is down you run the full poke loop, if it is up you treat 50% HP as your hard stop and never sit inside his lunge range.

notes: Warwick's Q and R are casts, so Blind does not touch them — the old text treated his whole kit as autos. Primal Howl (E) was absent from both layers despite being the ability that decides every mid-lane poke exchange.
